correctness.rationale: The ordered-uniform density transformed to minimum, range, and normalized interior coordinates factors as a product, proving endpoint-shape independence. Sample variance divided by squared range depends only on the normalized shape. Its mean is obtained exactly from two fixed endpoints and n-2 iid uniform interior points. Combining independence with the beta(n-1,2) range moments gives the stated covariance formula and strict positivity for q>0.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected range literature studies expectation bounds or deterministic range-versus-standard-deviation inequalities. The inspected 2026 source records the uniform beta range moments and general same-sample dependence but does not state the exact independence of S^2/R^2 from the endpoints or the resulting regression and covariance family. The normalized-spacing mechanism is classical in spirit, so the novelty claim is deliberately restricted to these variance consequences.
residual_risks: Classical uniform-spacing or invariant-statistic literature may encode the endpoint/normalized-shape independence in a form that makes the variance consequence immediate.
The main algebra after the shape factorization is elementary; originality rests on the specific independence/regression/covariance package rather than a new integration technique.
No claim is made for nonuniform continuous parent laws, where the factorization generally fails.

value.rationale: Sample range and sample variance are canonical dispersion summaries and are compared directly in classical range-standard-deviation theory. The exact endpoint-independent normalization gives a stronger structural relationship than a single covariance value, and the all-power covariance formula quantifies the resulting positive dependence for every sample size.
